title: Characterization of Gaussian Universality Breakdown in High-Dimensional Empirical Risk Minimization
claim: Matching low-order moments to a Gaussian surrogate predicts performance only in a special case; otherwise Gaussian universality breaks down.
layout: 3 panels: top error curve, bottom two score histograms, shared legends at right
description: The figure has a wide line plot on top and two histogram panels below, with legends at the right. The top plot shows test error against the loss-mixing parameter eta from 0 (l2 loss) to 1 (l1 loss). Blue solid curves with blue circles show predicted and empirical error for bimodal data. Green solid curves with green circles show the Gaussian surrogate. A dashed teal curve shows the prediction under the score-universality hypothesis. The blue and green curves start together at eta=0, then separate as eta grows. The dashed teal curve sits below both. The bottom row shows score histograms at eta=0. On the left, the bimodal data score has two sharp blue peaks, with a wide dashed Gaussian fit overlaid. On the right, the Gaussian surrogate score is a bell curve that matches its theoretical density. Bold titles carry the math notation.
caption: Breakdown of performance and score universality through an elastic loss. Top: Empirical generalization error and theoretical prediction for the teacher--student model $y=\theta^{*\top}x+\varepsilon$ as $\eta\in[0,1]$ varies, with $\mathcal L_y(t)=(1-\eta)(t-y)^2+\eta|t-y|$. The entries of $x$ are independent and bimodal, $\rho(\theta)=\|\theta\|_2^2$, $p=30$, and $n=50$. Performance universality is tested against Gaussian surrogate data with matching mean and covariance. Bottom: Score histograms at $\eta=0$, together with the theoretical prediction and a moment-matched Gaussian fit. Performance universality holds at the squared-loss endpoint $\eta=0$ although the score is non-Gaussian; for $\eta>0$, the moment-matched Gaussian surrogate no longer predicts the empirical performance.
abstract: We study high-dimensional convex empirical risk minimization (ERM) under general non-Gaussian data designs. By heuristically extending the Convex Gaussian Min-Max Theorem (CGMT) to non-Gaussian settings, we derive an asymptotic min-max characterization of key statistics, enabling approximation of the mean $Î¼_{\hatÎ¸}$ and covariance $C_{\hatÎ¸}$ of the ERM estimator $\hatÎ¸$. Specifically, under a concentration assumption on the data matrix and standard regularity conditions on the loss and regularizer, we show that for a test covariate $x$ independent of the training data, the projection $\hatÎ¸^\top x$ approximately follows the convolution of the generally non-Gaussian distribution of $Î¼_{\hatÎ¸}^\top x$ with an independent centered Gaussian variable of variance $\mathrm{tr}(C_{\hatÎ¸} \mathbb{E}[xx^\top])$. This result clarifies the scope and limits of Gaussian universality for ERMs. Numerical simulations across diverse losses and models are provided to validate our theoretical predictions and qualitative insights.
